field_changes.before: Would have created a broader TIF exception for districts containing qualified data centers.
field_changes.after: Failed proposal for WEDC-certified data-center TIF districts: except a district from the 12% equalized-value-limit findings requirement only when all project costs relate to an in-district qualified data center; prohibit later non-data-center project costs; and exclude excepted district value increments from other municipal TIF-limit calculations. Introduced AB228/SB241 operative texts match after documented normalization.

field_changes.before: Would have modified the qualified data center sales and use tax exemption and excluded cryptocurrency operations from the definition.
field_changes.after: Introduced sales/use-tax proposal revised qualified-data-center certification, including a separate colocation/rental-services alternative and a cryptocurrency exclusion. Recommended AB245 AA1 replaces that alternative with standalone/networked server computing for an owner, operator or tenant, for themselves or others; changes the crypto exclusion from AND to OR; restricts qualified-investment spending to the business entity specified in section238.40(1)(b) or its affiliate; and adds crypto-based certification revocation. SB244 SA1 has matching amendment instructions. Committee recommendation does not establish enactment; both bills failed.

field_changes.before: Would have required utility cost protections, onsite or directly accessible renewable resources, closed-loop cooling, annual water reporting, bonding, and reclamation for large data centers.
field_changes.after: Introduced AB840/SB843 proposed infrastructure-cost protections, onsite siting of renewable facilities primarily serving a data center, closed-loop cooling, annual water reports, bonding and reclamation. AB840 adopted ASA1 targets defined large data centers, expands protection to all utility costs, allows cooling using no more water than a closed loop, and ties restoration after permit expiry to municipal requirements. Its renewable-siting, cooling and bonding provisions exempt centers already operating or under construction on the proposed effective date. Offered SB843 SSA2 additionally proposes local approval of certain wind/solar projects; it is not treated as adopted. These are failed-bill terms.

field_changes.before: Statewide moratorium bill. It would have barred operation of data centers unless state law first created a planning authority, cost-shift protections, subsidy limits, public water and power reporting, pollution safeguards, renewable energy requirements, labor standards, NDA limits, local referendum approval, and enforcement provisions.
field_changes.after: Failed proposed operation moratorium for facilities primarily storing, managing and processing digital data that satisfy any one of: at least5000 servers, at least10000 square feet, or at least100MW demand. Operation would depend on all14 safeguards being provided by law, as determined by the DATCP secretary: planning authority, utility/infrastructure cost protections, recovery funding, subsidy elimination, water/energy reporting, pollution safeguards,100% newly built directly accessible renewables, construction wage standards, restored PSC planning, NDA restrictions, local referendum approval and enforcement. The referendum condition is a proposed legal prerequisite, not an observed ballot contest.

field_changes.before: Would have prohibited nondisclosure agreements intended to conceal data center information from the public, with trade-secret exceptions.
field_changes.after: Failed proposal barring political subdivisions and data centers or their agents from agreements, including NDAs, whose purpose or effect conceals development details or prevents public review. The exception is an agreement with the sole purpose of protecting a trade secret. A political subdivision could not permit or approve a data-center project while it or the center/agent violates the specified disclosure-agreement rules. Introduced SB969/AB1036 operative texts match after documented normalization.
